newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines -Mar 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines -Mar 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- The Education Department has decided to impose tough sanctions on public secondary schools that fail to use Chinese as the language of instruction from September next year.
-- U.S. Vice-president Al Gore arrived in Beijing and said he would not avoid discussing human rights issues with Chinese leaders.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Although the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group handling the handover failed to agree on when Chinese troops would enter Hong Kong, China has already decided to send its soldiers at dawn on July 1. They will be reviewed by Chinese leaders and post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Gore expressed hope that Sino-U.S. relations could be improved and stressed the importance of keeping a good relationship between the two countries.

-- Academics in Beijing warned of the possibility of pro-independence forces in Taiwan and Tibet joining forces. They said that by receiving the Dalai Lama, Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui had headed further down the road of Taiwan independence.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- A potential member of the Executive Council of the post-handover Special Administrative Region was ready to quit his positions in the private sector if Tung wanted to appoint him to head a taskforce on financial policies.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Chief Secretary Anson Chan will accompany Tung to Beijing this week to meet Chinese leaders -- the first time in her capacity as the Chief Executive-designate's right-hand woman.
-- Cosco Pacific, the listed arm of China's largest shipping company, sold $1.19 billion worth of new shares to buy stakes in ports in China and elsewhere in the region.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Disgraced former Chinese Communist Party chief Zhao Ziyang arrived in Shanghai over the weekend for his first visit after an absence from the public eye of nearly eight years.
